decision.summary: The Federal Reserve and other central banks announced the reestablishment of temporary U.S. dollar liquidity swap facilities to address funding strains in Europe.

changes.quote: In response to the reemergence of strains in U.S. dollar short-term funding markets in Europe, the Bank of Canada, the Bank of England, the European Central Bank, the Federal Reserve, and the Swiss National Bank are announcing the reestablishment of temporary U.S. dollar liquidity swap facilities.
changes.explanation: Global central banks are stepping in to provide U.S. dollar funding to help ease financial strains originating in Europe.

changes.quote: The arrangement with the Bank of Canada would support drawings of up to $30 billion, as was the case previously.
changes.explanation: The swap line with the Bank of Canada is set to support up to $30 billion, maintaining previous arrangements.

changes.quote: These swap arrangements have been authorized through January 2011.
changes.explanation: The temporary swap facilities are authorized to remain in place through January 2011.

tone_quotes.quote: These facilities are designed to help improve liquidity conditions in U.S. dollar funding markets and to prevent the spread of strains to other markets and financial centers.
Central banks will continue to work together closely as needed to address pressures in funding markets.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.26% APR costs about $59.42 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.45% and moved +12 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.06% would rise by about $22.14 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9.9%, and employers added an average of 106k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.2% over the past year (April 2010); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.6%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +4 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -1.03% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that central banks are ready to cooperate and provide liquidity to stabilize global funding markets as needed. An educational forecast model estimates an 87% chance of a hold at the next meeting.
